title: Traffic weighting & SLO priority labelling - POC scoping
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark guide + sampling templates (Alex) by 2026-04-02
Customer to provide 2 weeks of anonymized traffic profile (Diego) by 2026-04-06
Schedule first benchmark run (joint) week of 2026-04-13
action_items: Alex Mercer: share draft benchmark spreadsheet and traffic-weighting template (due 2026-04-02)
Diego Ramos: export and sanitize sample traffic + payload size distribution (due 2026-04-06)
Priya Shah: prepare runbook for first TTFT/TPOT sweep on Nucleus-1 GPU cluster (due 2026-04-09)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're here to align on the POC SLOs and how we'll measure them. Quick intros?
[00:12] Mike (CTO): Mike here, CTO at Calyx, Sara's sponsoring this, Diego is our ML lead. We're trying to validate feasibility for real-time note summarization in clinic workflows. Latency is critical.
[00:25] Sara (Platform PM): Hi all, we care about first-response latency for UI snappiness and also overall cost per session.
[00:35] Alex: Great. Priya will lead the technical bits.
[00:38] Priya (SE): hi, thanks. quick overview: we want to decide TTFT (time to first token) versus TPOT (total per token) targets, set p95/p99 thresholds, and define sampling so the benchmarks are representative. we'll propose a hybrid SLO.
[00:56] Diego (ML Eng): quick interruption: our production traffic has a wide payload variance — from 30 tokens up to 4k tokens — but median is ~240. also 15% of sessions are multi-turn.
[01:12] Priya: that's helpful, Diego. so for SLOs we usually recommend separating two axes: TTFT sensitivity for interactive UI flows (goal: perceived latency) and TPOT for cost and throughput budgeting.
[01:28] Mike: what's the typical p95 you'd set for TTFT on similar customers?
[01:33] Priya: it depends on model/hardware combination. for our hosted small-chat workloads we often see p95 TTFT ~120-180ms on high-end GPUs; p99 can be 250-400ms. but with long prompts and kv cache misses, it goes up. for TPOT we think in aggregated per-token multiples, e.g., p95 tokens/sec targets or per-session median TOT.
[01:56] Sara: we need concrete targets for procurement. can we map to our acceptance criteria?
[02:02] Alex: yes. proposal: define two primary acceptance criteria: 1) Interactive SLO: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, TTFT p99 <= 450ms for the 90% traffic slice (see weighting) 2) Throughput/cost SLO: average token cost per session within X relative to baseline, and sustained TPOT p95 throughput of Y tokens/sec on reserved capacity.
[02:26] Diego: that 90% traffic slice, how do we define it? our tails are heavy — there are occasional 4k prompts that skew metrics.
[02:34] Priya: we recommend traffic weighting: carve traffic into buckets (short < 512, medium 512-2048, long > 2048) and allocate sampling weights based on production proportions but cap long-prompt influence for TTFT SLOs. so TTFT SLOs evaluate on short+medium mostly while TPOT uses full distribution.
[02:56] Mike: so you're basically saying we'll prioritize TTFT for the short flows since that's the UX-critical piece?
[03:01] Priya: Exactly. UX-critical flows get the TTFT SLA. For TPOT we measure overall per-token latency and throughput across complete traffic.
[03:09] Sara: what about p99? Do we accept higher p99 for long prompts?
[03:13] Priya: Yes. proposal: TTFT p95 <= 250ms on short+medium; TTFT p99 <= 600ms on combined traffic but annotate that long prompts are excluded from hard-fail. we call those "SLO guardrails" rather than hard SLOs.
[03:28] Diego: makes sense. what about measurement approach — active vs passive?
[03:32] Alex: We'll do a mixed approach. Passive measurement from live traffic (post-sanitization) to validate real-world numbers, plus active benchmark sweeps with controlled payloads to isolate TTFT/TPOT across model variants and hardware.
[03:47] Priya: for active runs we'll use three payload profiles: short (60-256 tokens), medium (257-1024), long (1025-4096). each sweep will measure TTFT distribution, steady-state token throughput with batching, and end-to-end tokens/second. we'll run sweeps across target hardware: Nucleus-1 (A100-equivalent), Nucleus-2 (H100-equivalent), and a quantized CPU baseline.
[04:16] Mike: timeline for these runs?
[04:18] Priya: rough plan: client provides 2 weeks of traffic by 2026-04-06, we produce initial sampling and weighting proposal by 2026-04-02; first active sweep in week of 2026-04-13; analysis and refinement by 2026-04-20; pilot acceptance decision by 2026-04-30.
[04:36] Sara: procurement needs a clear acceptance checkbox. can you show what "pass" looks like?
[04:41] Alex: pass criteria (draft): 1) TTFT p95 <= 250ms for weighted short+medium sample, p99 <= 550ms for same slice. 2) End-to-end session success rate >= 99.5% (no failures/timeouts). 3) Cost per 1k tokens within 20% of benchmarked baseline on dedicated capacity. 4) No regressions in quality metrics (we'll run eval prompts).
[05:07] Diego: how do you measure success rate? does that include partial generation errors?
[05:11] Priya: success rate includes no server errors, model OOMs, or truncated responses beyond our truncation policy. partial generation due to prompt overdose counts as an edge-case and we log separately.
[05:22] Mike: curious about what tooling you'll give us to run passive measurement? we don't want to send raw PII traces.
[05:28] Alex: we'll give a redact+hash script and a telemetry schema. Redwood only needs latencies, payload token counts, and some light labels (is_multi_turn boolean, user_agent). No raw text. link: doc: https://redwood.internal/poc/telemetry-redact (shared).
[05:46] Sara: ok good. can you outline benchmark matrix? I want to see combinations and expected time per sweep.
[05:52] Priya: benchmark matrix: 3 payload profiles x 3 models (open-llama-13b, redwood-curie-7b, redwood-claude-ish) x 3 infra types x 5 concurrency points (1,4,8,16,32) x 3 runs each. Each sweep ~2-4 hours per infra/model combo. We'll parallelize a bit but expect first round ~2 days to complete.
[06:18] Diego: that seems heavy. can you prioritize combos so we don't burn credits?
[06:22] Priya: yes — we'll prioritize the model variant you plan to run in production (you said model A earlier?), and run a smaller matrix for others. we can also do tiered runs: TTFT first on short payloads, then TPOT with aggregated runs.
[06:35] Mike: what about canary/fallback strategies if dedicated capacity has an outage?
[06:39] Alex: part of the POC we'll test fallbacks: ability to route to hosted standby model, and automatic degrade of batch size to preserve TTFT. we'll log degradations as incidents but still maintain the UX SLO where possible.
[06:52] Sara: someone asked earlier about percentiles for costs, not just latency. do you compute cost p95?
[06:57] Priya: We report cost distributions per session and per token, so yes, cost p95 and cost per 1k tokens. that helps procurement compare committed versus burst behave.
[07:07] Diego: about sampling: how do you weight rare but business-critical flows? some long prompts are high value (clinical summaries).
[07:13] Priya: we recommend priority tags: label high-value traffic and ensure they have representation in the evaluation even if they are rare. in the sampling template we'll include a weighted bucket for "priority long" with a small but guaranteed sample.
[07:26] Mike: congrats, that's good. any blockers we foresee?
[07:29] Alex: blockers: A) sanitized traffic export B) access to your staging network for benchmark harness C) agreement on model variant and infra for initial runs. all resolvable.
[07:40] Sara: on staging access, Diego will coordinate with infra, but we need a lightweight harness. can Redwood provide a containerized runner?
[07:46] Priya: yes — we'll supply a dockerized runner and runbook. Priya: I'll also include terraform snippets optional for dedicated pool sizing.
[07:56] Diego: one last nuance — we want to measure tail latency when KV cache is warmed vs cold. can you capture both?
[08:03] Priya: absolutely. active sweeps will include cold-start sequences and warmed runs; we'll note cache hit rates and separate TTFT for warm/cold.
[08:13] Alex: ok let's recap next steps — Alex to share benchmark guide and template, Diego to provide sanitized traffic, Priya to prepare runbook and infra plan, schedule run week of 2026-04-13.
[08:28] Mike: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:30] Sara: thanks.
[08:31] Outro
